terms.display_name: Which data-quality checks should this database have?
terms.description: propose_quality_checks reads the measured value profile and, for every column and table, applies the selection rules to propose a check, each in an Egeria quality dimension: Completeness (is the value there: Required, Missing_Pct, Required_No_Placeholder and Row_Ct_Pct), Uniqueness (Unique), Timeliness (Future_Date) and Conformity (Min_Date). A person accepts or rejects each proposal in Curate; a check whose inputs were not measured is listed as not established with the reason, never silently left out.
terms.summary: A data owner cannot ask for quality until someone says what to check, and writing the checks by hand for hundreds of tables never gets done.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Which data-quality checks hold on this database's tables, and which fail?
terms.description: run_quality_checks runs the checks a person accepted, one aggregate query per table, and records pass, warning or fail per check, or not established with the reason (an empty table, a zero baseline, a column that has gone) and never a pass for a measure that is undefined. Each evaluated check is published as one Egeria QualityAnnotation in its dimension: Completeness (is the value there: Required, Missing_Pct, Required_No_Placeholder and Row_Ct_Pct), Uniqueness (Unique), Timeliness (Future_Date) and Conformity (Min_Date). With no accepted check the step is not run ("no accepted checks"), never an empty report.
terms.summary: A check nobody runs is a wish; the steward needs to see which accepted checks pass, warn or fail, and which could not be evaluated.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Any known feedback?
terms.description: RE's Curate intent already holds resource_feedback for cataloged resources.
terms.summary: Other experts, reduces risk if positive.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Are there any restrictions for use beyond the license — classification, zone or terms of use?
terms.description: Separated from the license question itself when that one became cross-type and moved to Scouting. Reads Egeria governance zones and classifications, the resource's own terms-of-use text, and Enrichment for anything contractual that is not written down machine-readably.
terms.summary: A permissive license does not mean an internal classification, a governance zone or a contractual term allows the use I have in mind.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Are there outstanding CVEs?
terms.description: Covers advisories against DECLARED dependencies only, queried from OSV.dev, with coverage reported as prominently as the count — so a zero is 'none found in what we can see', not 'none exist'.
terms.summary: Understand the risk.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Are there views, materialised views, functions or triggers that encode business logic?
terms.description: The DDL is already in the catalog (pg_views, pg_matviews, pg_proc, pg_trigger) and Resource Explorer already parses view DDL with SQLGlot for dependencies, column lineage and complexity. What is missing is the link from that step's output back to the question layer.
terms.summary: Logic hidden in views and triggers is logic no application-level survey will ever find.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Based on what's already known, is this worth investigating further, or should it be deprioritized?
terms.description: Disposition control (Track/Investigate/Recommend/Abandon/Ignore) plus history — the same repo_dispositions state Scouting already exposes, now reachable directly from Discovery too.
terms.summary: Discovery-tier signal (license risk, maturity, conventions) is exactly the point a go/no-go call should get made and recorded, not lost.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Can Egeria's survey engine reach this resource, or must Resource Explorer survey it locally — and which is cheaper?
terms.description: Reachability is testable by running the native survey with finalAnalysisStep=CHECK_ASSET from the engine host; efficiency is a separate axis (data locality, latency to first result, load on the source, concurrency, provenance) — see multi-resource-questions-design.md §3 rule B. An unreachable resource falls back to a Resource Explorer local mirror published under the native annotation shapes, plus an RFA recording that Egeria could not reach it.
terms.summary: Whether a survey can run at all, and where it runs, decides the cost and the provenance of every answer that follows.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Could this be in scope for what I am looking for — worth the full pass?
terms.description: design §16.3's Discovery gate and §16.5 point 2 — fit is a query over stored measurements, not a survey, so changing the requirement recomputes fit across every already-surveyed resource at zero fetch cost, and the same question works with no requirement at all as a comparison across resources.
terms.summary: This is the gate: it decides whether the Analysis-tier aggregate pass is worth paying for on this resource, from signals that cost nothing.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Do we already support these dependencies?
terms.description: Needs the org's own tech inventory — human-supplied cross-reference, not resource-derivable.
terms.summary: Reduces risk.
terms.usage: Typically relevant during Analysis and Enrichment.

terms.display_name: Do we have the skills to support its use?
terms.description: Purely human-supplied — never resource-derivable.
terms.summary: Operational readiness and skill gaps.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Enrichment.

terms.display_name: Do we know what the cost to run it is?
terms.description: Human-supplied/derived — not resource-derivable.
terms.summary: Cost is part of the decision process.
terms.usage: Typically relevant during Analysis and Enrichment.

terms.display_name: Does it fit into our governance frameworks?
terms.description: Org policy cross-reference (human-supplied), plus Curate's zone/catalog membership once published.
terms.summary: Compliance and regulatory alignment.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Enrichment.

terms.display_name: Does it fit into our monitoring infrastructure?
terms.description: Org-internal cross-reference — human-supplied.
terms.summary: Cost, Skills and manageability.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Enrichment.

terms.display_name: Does it fit into our security infrastructure?
terms.description: An organisation-internal cross-reference: the security findings inform it, a person answers it.
terms.summary: Will it be allowed in? What are the risks?
terms.usage: Typically relevant during Analysis and Enrichment.

terms.display_name: Does it hold an OpenSSF Best Practices (CII) badge, and how current is the self-assessment behind it?
terms.description: cii_badge reads the real badge from bestpractices.dev rather than estimating one, and reports level together with the age of the self-assessment. No question referenced it.
terms.summary: A badge is a public claim by the project about itself; its age tells me how much the claim is still worth.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: Does it replace or extend something we already have?
terms.description: Answerable locally from RE's own registry/groups, same as "existing use within our organization."
terms.summary: Duplication can be costly - needs to be factored in.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Does the repository have automated build tooling in place?
terms.description: Covers whether build tooling configuration is present and whether CI actually runs, tests and gates.
terms.summary: Independent of CI wiring — a Makefile/build.gradle/pyproject build-system table means it can be built locally even if CI is absent or broken.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Does the repository publish a clear process for reporting security vulnerabilities?
terms.description: Reads SECURITY.md's content for an actual disclosure process, not just the file's presence — which is reported separately.
terms.summary: Knowing how to responsibly disclose a finding — and whether maintainers take security seriously — matters before we rely on this.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Does the software contain telemetry, phone-home mechanisms, or external metrics tracking?
terms.description: Matches known telemetry and analytics SDK imports and endpoints in source, and separately checks whether each match is disclosed in the repo's own docs. An undisclosed match is the finding, not the presence of telemetry.
terms.summary: Prevents unauthorized leakage of internal network metadata, system details, or usage patterns.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Does this filesystem contain recognizable tabular or structured data files, and what do their schemas look like?
terms.description: filesystem_inventory profiles tabular data file schemas (CSV, Excel, Parquet) it recognizes during the same walk — this reuses that profiling rather than a separate pass.
terms.summary: Whether a filesystem holds usable structured data determines whether it's worth treating as a dataset source.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Does this fit within or need to extend our existing infrastructure estate?
terms.description: Org-internal cross-reference — human-supplied.
terms.summary: Impact on existing architecture and operations.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Enrichment.

terms.display_name: For AI/ML assets, what licensing or usage constraints apply to models, weights, or datasets?
terms.description: Needs model-card/dataset-file detection — real gap, AI Governance tooling category.
terms.summary: Open-source software licenses (e.g., Apache 2.0) often differ from model weights (e.g., OpenRAIL, Llama) or training data constraints.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Has this resource already been catalogued in Egeria, and when?
terms.description: "Known inventory" check — is there already a catalog asset for this repo, independent of whether it's registered in Resource Explorer's own local registry. Ties to the Scouting "shop for data" search work.
terms.summary: Has someone already done this analysis? What did they learn?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Has this resource already been surveyed at any tier, and what did earlier signals reveal?
terms.description: Direct field — last_surveyed_at, is_published (egeria_asset_guid), and any locally-cached findings/metrics history already surfaced by the resource's own analysis cards.
terms.summary: Avoid re-deriving what's already known; ground the decision in prior signal instead of starting cold.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: How big is this database — schemas, tables, views, columns, rows and bytes?
terms.description: Whole-database catalog reads only, no row data: information_schema and pg_catalog give the structural counts, and relation sizes plus row counts give the volume. Design §5.1 — extract everything the catalog already knows before reading a row.
terms.summary: Size sets the cost of every later tier, and is the first thing that says whether this is a toy or a production estate.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: How complete and consistent is this database's documentation?
terms.description: Scores the coverage measure against criteria and adds the convention checks — a database where every table has a comment but half of them repeat the table name is not well documented.
terms.summary: Documentation coverage is the scored version of the Scouting comment question, and the one a steward is measured on.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: How concentrated is authorship — would the project survive losing its top contributors?
terms.description: chaoss_metrics reports the elephant factor and related CHAOSS metrics on their own terms, never averaged into a score. No question referenced it.
terms.summary: A healthy commit rate produced by one person is a different risk from the same rate produced by twenty.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: How do its components relate to each other?
terms.description: Split from the combined 'internal architecture' question 2026-09-08 (Dan: is a separate question worth splitting out; chat-facts rendering cannot flatten a component graph into bullet text at any real scale, so this half needs its own answer, not a share of the other one's). architecture_diagram is the Mermaid diagram + caption rendered from architecture_recovery/architecture_summary at survey time -- previously computed and persisted, never read back by anything.
terms.summary: I need to know what I would be taking on before committing to it, and whether its own documentation matches what the code actually does.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: How does it score against OpenSSF Scorecard-style criteria?
terms.description: foss_scorecard computes Scorecard-shaped checks from data already collected — it is NOT the upstream OpenSSF tool's own run, and a check it cannot evaluate is reported as not-established rather than as a failure.
terms.summary: A named, comparable rubric is what lets me weigh several candidates against each other rather than judging each on its own terms.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: How does the repository handle secrets, credentials, and sensitive configurations?
terms.description: Runs a vendored gitleaks ruleset over the HEAD snapshot of tracked files, naming the ruleset and commit. Never claims 'no secrets' — only 'no matches against this ruleset, in this snapshot' — and says nothing about git history, where a removed secret still lives.
terms.summary: Prevents hardcoded secrets or unencrypted credential passing in containerized and automated deployment environments.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: How is it supported?
terms.description: Combines community responsiveness, documentation quality and any formal support documents.
terms.summary: Enterprise fallback and support options.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: How is this database changing — rows inserted, updated and deleted per table per period, size drift and schema churn?
terms.description: Deltas of the n_tup_ins/upd/del counters and of relation sizes between two stored snapshots, per table, producing a series the Understanding tier can chart and the change detectors in design §9 can threshold. Depends on the structured per-snapshot tables, not on re-parsing the survey JSON blob.
terms.summary: A point-in-time survey cannot distinguish a busy table from an abandoned one; the deltas can.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: How mature is it?
terms.description: Direct lifecycle-stage classification (nascent/emerging/established/mature) from repo_created_at, CHAOSS-informed (the maturity analysis) — a more direct answer than the age/release-cadence trend chart alone, which remains a secondary Understanding-tier view of the same underlying signal.
terms.summary: Stability vs innovation trade-off.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: How much code is there? How complex?
terms.description: Both halves are answerable as of 2026-09-02. SIZE: language_file_classification carries a per-language line census — code, comment, docstring and blank — written at ingestion and at Coarse Profile refresh (pipeline.py::_record_line_census). Markdown, JSON, HTML, CSS, SQL and XML are counted as text and excluded from the code total by construction; project_stats.ingestion_lines_of_code, which counted every newline in every text file and reported 1,118,195 against ~156k real code lines on egeria-python, is retired and must not be cited. COMPLEXITY: api_structure carries the per-language max/mean it always computed, python and java only — go and javascript store 0 for every symbol because their extractors never compute it, so they are excluded and named rather than averaged in (0.32 vs 2.69 on milvus). A repo with no census reports no line counts rather than zero: not counted is not the same as no code.
terms.summary: Gives an estimate on cost to maintain.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: How much has changed since the last time this was surveyed — is it worth re-running now?
terms.description: notification_detector.py's latest-two-runs comparison, surfaced via an Automate subscription once a schedule exists for the analysis — real today, but only reachable once that subscription is set up.
terms.summary: Re-surveying on a blind schedule wastes cycles; knowing whether anything material actually changed first is the real Discovery-tier judgment.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: How well documented is it?
terms.description: Covers root README, CHANGELOG and CONTRIBUTING presence with a quality label, plus whole-tree density — README count, a docs folder, .md/.txt count.
terms.summary: Ease of adoption and maintenance.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: How well-governed is this database's reference data — what share of its low-cardinality columns are bound to a set?
terms.description: The denominator is the columns whose cardinality makes them reference-data candidates; the numerator is those bound to an Egeria ValidValueSet. Both come from the reference-data matching analysis.
terms.summary: Reference-data governance is measurable as a share, which makes it one of the few governance claims that can be tracked over time.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: How well-modelled is this database — keys, constraints, foreign-key coverage, orphan tables and grain clarity?
terms.description: Scores the convention checks together with grain clarity: a table whose grain cannot be stated is a modelling defect even when its constraints are all present.
terms.summary: Modelling quality predicts how expensive this database will be to integrate with anything else.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: How widely adopted and active is the community around this repository?
terms.description: Stars are attention, not community. community_support reports the dimensions separately and names the weakest rather than averaging, so 'popular but unsupported' stays visible instead of averaging out.
terms.summary: Reduces adoption risk, provides a health proxy, and ensures community support and responsiveness.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: Is intellectual property (IP) provenance managed via CLA or DCO?
terms.description: Reports which mechanism is in use — DCO sign-off in commit trailers, a CLA bot configuration, or a CONTRIBUTING.md statement — rather than a yes/no.
terms.summary: Protects the organization from copyright infringement claims from unauthorized third-party contributions.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Is there a Survey Definition authored for this resource's technology type at all, or is that a catalog gap?
terms.description: Direct field — the candidates list itself; an empty result for a technology type with real registered resources is the signal.
terms.summary: A resource type with no Survey Definition authored yet is itself a real, actionable finding — a catalog gap someone should close — not a silent empty list.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Is there a current, published, security analysis?
terms.description: Not answered — a published third-party audit is a different artifact from these checks, and nothing detects one.
terms.summary: Third-party audit and security posture.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Is there a data model here — do the tables relate through foreign keys, or is this a bag of tables?
terms.description: Zero new fetch: the foreign-key constraints Scouting already read become a graph, and the measure is connectivity — orphan tables, components, in-degree.
terms.summary: A database with no declared relationships needs a very different kind of attention from one with a real model.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Is there a defined need or market for this resource — subscriptions, requests, existing use, feedback or open requests for this kind of data?
terms.description: Reads Egeria DigitalSubscription, Resource Explorer's own registry of existing use and feedback, similar-resource search hits, and open RFAs asking for this kind of data. Design §4 requires this and the readiness question to hold together before a DigitalProduct is proposed.
terms.summary: The demand half: building a data product nobody asked for costs more than it returns.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: Is there a validation / deployment test for it?
terms.description: Covers whether CI runs tests and whether deployment evidence exists; a real deployment validation test is not detected.
terms.summary: How do we know if it is working properly once deployed?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Is there any existing use within our organization?
terms.description: Answerable locally from RE's own registry (cross-reference against already-registered repos/groups) — no external API needed.
terms.summary: Other experts, reduces risk if successful. Dependencies already in place, etc.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Is there any reliability or availability aspects?
terms.description: Trend/uptime signal, if available — Understanding-tier chart, or Analysis if content-derived (SLA docs).
terms.summary: Is it production ready?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Is this a copy, subset or superset of a resource we already know — structurally, by schema or file signature?
terms.description: A schema signature — table and column names, types, key structure — hashed into a fingerprint and compared against the fingerprints of databases already in the registry. Egeria's FingerprintAnnotation is the publication shape.
terms.summary: Paying to survey, host and govern the third copy of the same database is a cost nobody decided to take on.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Is this database a primary or a replica, is it clustered, and is WAL archiving or backup configured?
terms.description: Catalog-observable: pg_is_in_recovery() for the primary/standby role, pg_stat_replication for standbys and replay lag, pg_settings.archive_mode with pg_stat_archiver for WAL archiving, pg_extension and roles for backup tooling such as pgBackRest, barman or wal-g, Citus catalogs for clustering. Design §5.5 — last successful backup and tested restore are NOT observable and are asked separately.
terms.summary: Whether the data survives a failure is a property of the deployment, not of the schema, and nothing else in a survey reveals it.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: Is this database alive — writes since the statistics were reset, last vacuum or analyse, and is anything reading it?
terms.description: pg_stat_user_tables carries n_tup_ins/upd/del, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_vacuum/autovacuum/analyze, seq_scan and idx_scan; pg_stat_database carries the transaction and block counters. All of it is a catalog read. Note the two absence modes design §5.1 calls out: a counter the engine does not support is not_established, and statistics that were never collected must render as "run ANALYZE", not as "no activity".
terms.summary: A database nobody writes to and nobody reads is a retirement candidate, not a survey candidate.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: Is this database documented — what fraction of its tables and columns carry comments?
terms.description: pg_description via obj_description and col_description gives comments per table and per column; the measure is coverage, not presence. Note rule 13 in the package CLAUDE.md — these need the schema-qualified (schema.table)::regclass form.
terms.summary: Undocumented tables are the single biggest obstacle to anyone reusing a database they did not build.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: Is this database maintained and healthy — vacuum recency, dead-tuple ratio and unused indexes?
terms.description: Scores the activity signals against thresholds: how long since the last vacuum or analyse, the ratio of dead to live tuples, and indexes that have never been scanned. Remember design §5.1's absence rule — statistics that were never collected must not read as a healthy zero.
terms.summary: Operational neglect shows up in the statistics long before it shows up as an outage.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: Is this database resilient — replica present, archiving on, backup evidence and a tested restore?
terms.description: Design §5.5 makes this deliberately two-sided: the catalog facts (role, replicas, archiving, backup tooling) and the Enrichment facts (last successful backup, tested restore, RPO and RTO). The envelope must say which half answered, because a green score drawn only from the catalog half would claim something nobody verified.
terms.summary: A data owner signing off on a database is signing off on its recovery, not its schema.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: Is this repository actively maintained?
terms.description: Recency/frequency signal — last-pushed date, commit cadence — answerable from GitHub API metadata alone (RE's HealthSurveyor), no zipball needed.
terms.summary: I don't want to start using something that is a dead-end burden.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: Is this repository already self-described for an enterprise catalog (e.g. Backstage catalog-info.yaml)?
terms.description: repo_conventions detects catalog-info.yaml and equivalent self-description files. Same parser problem — the row was wired correctly and phrased in a way the generator read as unknown.
terms.summary: A strong, cheap signal that this repo is already integrated into some enterprise inventory, independent of which catalog it names.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: Is this resource ready to be offered as a data product — owner, description, license or agreement, schema, freshness, contact and scope?
terms.description: A composite over facts other questions already establish — Egeria Ownership, a description, License or DataSharingAgreement, a schema, freshness signals, a contact and a DataScope. Design §4 requires this and the demand question to hold together before a DigitalProduct is proposed.
terms.summary: The supply half of a data product: one with no accountable owner, no license and no stated scope cannot responsibly be offered.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: Under what license or agreement may this resource be used?
terms.description: License field is cheaply available from the GitHub API — deeper copyleft-risk categorization is Assessment-tier (see the license-specifics row below).
terms.summary: Is this appropriate?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: What APIs and code symbols does it expose to callers?
terms.description: Covers the extracted code symbols and the interfaces implied by dependencies; a published contract is detected only where a specification file exists.
terms.summary: The published surface is what we would actually be coupling to, and what breaks on upgrade.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What are the public interfaces?
terms.description: interface_surface detects which interface styles a repo exposes (http_api, grpc, graphql, messaging, soap, cli) and whether a contract is actually published, versus merely implied by a dependency. Discovery altitude: 'is there a published contract' rather than 'what symbols exist', which is the Analysis-stage question 'What APIs and code symbols does it expose to callers?' (api_structure + interface_surface).
terms.summary: How do we use this - does it look like it does what we want?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: What components exist in this repository, and what kind is each?
terms.description: architecture_recovery, architecture_summary and architecture_doc_lens all exist; no question referenced any of them. The doc lens specifically compares documented architecture against recovered architecture.
terms.summary: I need to know what I would be taking on before committing to it, and whether its own documentation matches what the code actually does.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: What data files does it ship, and what shape are they?
terms.description: An inventory and shape profile of the data files shipped in the repository.
terms.summary: Bundled data can carry licensing and privacy obligations that the repo's own licence does not cover.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What dependencies does this require?
terms.description: The declared dependency list, per ecosystem, from the manifests present.
terms.summary: Influences deployment cost and exposes additional transitive risks.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What deployment styles does this support?
terms.description: Covers whether a Dockerfile, compose file or Helm chart is present. What the deployment instructions actually say is not read.
terms.summary: Need to understand if we can deploy it?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What do the columns actually contain — nulls, distinct counts, most-common values, ranges and widths?
terms.description: pg_stats, populated by ANALYZE, already carries null_frac, n_distinct, most_common_vals, most_common_freqs, histogram_bounds, avg_width and correlation — column profiling with no sampling at all. Value sampling is the fallback for columns whose statistics are stale or missing. Design §5.8: the answer envelope must state which route ran and, when sampled, the strategy, bound and seed.
terms.summary: Types say what a column may hold; only the values say what it does hold.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What does this database depend on outside itself — foreign data wrappers, dblink, extensions or publications?
terms.description: pg_foreign_server and pg_foreign_table for FDWs, pg_extension for extensions including dblink, pg_publication and pg_subscription for logical replication. A catalog read, no row data.
terms.summary: An external dependency is a reachability, security and upgrade constraint that the schema alone never shows.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What does this resource cost to run, host or license?
terms.description: Human-supplied/derived — not resource-derivable.
terms.summary: Cost is part of the decision process.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Enrichment.

terms.display_name: What engine and version is this, which extensions are installed, and is the version still supported?
terms.description: Server-level rather than database-level — design §5 makes server, database, schema and table each addressable, and this row belongs to the server subset. Sources: version(), pg_settings, pg_extension, and the upstream support window for the major version.
terms.summary: An unsupported engine version is a security and upgrade liability before anything about the data matters.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: What explicit license does this resource use, and are there non-standard or copyleft terms?
terms.description: GitHub API license field gives the SPDX id cheaply (Scouting); license_classification (Assessment) categorizes it into a risk tier (permissive/weak copyleft/strong copyleft/source-available/unknown) — candidate reference tools for deeper provenance: FOSSology (Linux Foundation compliance workspace), LicenseFinder, ClearlyDefined (crowdsourced licensing/provenance data), Mend, Black Duck. SPDX (ISO/IEC 5962) is the standard schema this conforms to.
terms.summary: Identifies strict copyleft (GPL/AGPL), source-available shifts (BSL/SSPL), or dual-licensing risks before code integration.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: What is inside the JSON, JSONB and XML columns — keys, nesting, types, and consistency across rows?
terms.description: JSONB via jsonb_object_keys and jsonb_typeof over a bounded sample, giving key frequency, nesting depth and type consistency across rows; XML via the root element and xpath key sampling. The result is a SchemaAnalysisAnnotation carrying an inferred nested schema, sharing its inference core with the filesystem path's JSON and XML file profiling.
terms.summary: A schema that stops at "jsonb" describes the column and says nothing about the data.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What is its internal architecture — what components exist and how do they relate?
terms.description: architecture_recovery, architecture_summary and architecture_doc_lens all exist; no question referenced any of them. The doc lens specifically compares documented architecture against recovered architecture.
terms.summary: I need to know what I would be taking on before committing to it, and whether its own documentation matches what the code actually does.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: What is the full schema — tables, columns, types, keys, constraints and indexes?
terms.description: The complete catalog read: information_schema and pg_catalog for schemas, tables, columns and types; pg_constraint for primary, foreign, unique and check constraints; pg_index for indexes. Published under Egeria's own Relational* metric keys so a native and a local run are comparable (design §2.2).
terms.summary: The schema is the contract, and every structural question downstream is asked against it.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What is the grain of each table — one row per what?
terms.description: Inferred from primary-key composition, column names, n_distinct approaching the row count, and date columns — emitted as an Egeria DataGrainAnnotation with a grainStatement and a confidence. Shared with the filesystem path, where the same inference runs over a data file's columns.
terms.summary: Grain is the first thing a consumer has to know and the last thing most databases write down.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: What is the scope of the data in time — collection period, validity and coverage?
terms.description: The other half of DataScope, and machine-proposable for most types: minimum and maximum of date columns for a database, modification-time range and in-file date ranges for a filesystem, DCAT temporal for a published dataset. Human confirmation of validity and coverage comes through Enrichment.
terms.summary: A consumer needs to know which period the data actually covers before trusting any answer drawn from it.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What is the sensitive-data exposure — which sensitive columns can which roles read?
terms.description: The scored form of the access-and-sensitivity question in Analysis: sensitive columns identified by Data Class matching, crossed with who holds read access to them, weighted by the breadth of the grant. A PUBLIC grant on a column of personal data is the finding this exists to surface.
terms.summary: This is the question a privacy review actually asks, and it is a cross of two analyses rather than either one.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

terms.display_name: What is the upgrade process?
terms.description: Needs content read (CHANGELOG, release notes) — RAG-tier, real gap.
terms.summary: Is it deployable and maintainable? Are upgrades disruptive?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What is this data about — which subjects, business terms or data classes does it appear to hold?
terms.description: Free at Scouting cost (design §16.2): table and column names plus pg_description comments already sit in RE's stored rows, so candidate subject terms need no new fetch. Confidence is low-medium on purpose — §16.2's "a name is a claim".
terms.summary: A consumer shopping for data searches by subject, not by table name; a resource nobody can describe is a resource nobody finds.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: What is this resource, and what is it for?
terms.description: Purpose/description — from the repo's own GitHub description field, no deeper analysis required.
terms.summary: Need to understand it to use it appropriately.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: What kind of database is this — transactional, analytical, reference data, staging or a copy?
terms.description: Zero new fetch — reasons over what Scouting already stored: table shapes, foreign-key density, naming conventions, read/write ratios from the tuple counters, and the query mix if pg_stat_statements is installed.
terms.summary: The kind of database decides which later analyses are worth paying for at all.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: What kind of thing is this repository — a library, an application, a tool, or samples?
terms.description: repo_classification exists and nothing asked for it. It also decides whether architecture recovery is worth running, so it gates later tiers.
terms.summary: The same signal means different things depending on what the repo is; a tutorial with no tests is fine, a library with none is not.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: What kinds of files does this filesystem contain, and how much data is there?
terms.description: File walk classifies every file by format and type, records sizes and timestamps — RE's baseline inventory for a filesystem resource, the filesystem equivalent of schema_inventory for a database.
terms.summary: Need a basic inventory before deciding whether deeper analysis of this filesystem is worth the time.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: What kinds of integrations does it support?
terms.description: Covers which interfaces exist and whether they are documented. Which named third-party systems it integrates with is not read.
terms.summary: Can we connect it to our ecosystem?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: What languages and file types make up this repository?
terms.description: language_file_classification is one of the oldest analyses here and no question referenced it.
terms.summary: Language mix is the cheapest signal of whether this is something we can maintain in-house.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: What period and places does this appear to cover, from catalog statistics and names alone?
terms.description: design §16.2: pg_stats histogram bounds give a date column's min and max WITHOUT reading rows. Its own warning is the load-bearing part — "absent means 'run ANALYZE', not 'no dates'" — so the two states are separately named rather than collapsed.
terms.summary: Data that does not cover the period or the places being asked about is out of scope however good it is, and finding that out after the expensive pass is the waste the funnel exists to avoid.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: When was this resource last backed up successfully, and has a restore ever been tested?
terms.description: Design §5.5 draws the line explicitly for databases: primary/standby role, replicas, WAL archiving and extension-based backup tooling are catalog-observable, while last successful backup, tested restore and RPO/RTO are not, for any resource type. They come from an Enrichment "Backup and recovery" section, and the answer envelope must say which half answered.
terms.summary: These are the two resilience questions a data owner actually asks, and the two that nothing inside the resource itself can answer.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Enrichment.

terms.display_name: Where is this resource physically located, under which jurisdiction, and are there residency or transfer constraints?
terms.description: Two halves. The machine half reads host and region from the connection endpoint, cloud instance metadata, or the mount and file path. The human half — legal controller, residency rule — comes through Enrichment. The result is published as a proposed Egeria DataScope classification carrying scopeElements {jurisdiction, region, controller}.
terms.summary: Data sovereignty decides whether we may hold or process this at all, independently of what the license permits.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Which Survey Definition should I run — a quick coarse check or the full deep survey?
terms.description: Survey Definitions carry their own step lists/descriptions and survey_kind tag; the Discovery candidates list surfaces exactly this per-step breakdown before committing to run one.
terms.summary: Running the wrong tier wastes time (full survey when a coarse check would do) or leaves real gaps (coarse-only when depth was actually needed) — the choice should be informed, not default.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Which columns conform to a known Data Class, with what confidence, and which look like a class we do not have yet?
terms.description: Generalises the existing PII matching: column name, type and sampled value patterns matched against every Egeria DataClass, producing a DataClassAnnotation per column with a stated confidence. Columns that show a clear pattern but match nothing raise an RFA proposing a new Data Class, carrying the observed pattern. Per design §5.8 the confidence is always stated against the sample, never as an unqualified "conforms".
terms.summary: Knowing where the sensitive data actually sits is the precondition for every privacy and access question after it.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Which columns hold semi-structured data (JSON, JSONB, XML, arrays or hstore), and how much of the data sits in them?
terms.description: Zero new fetch — the column types are already in the catalog read; what is derived is which columns are semi-structured and what share of the stored bytes they account for. The contents themselves are a separate, more expensive Analysis question.
terms.summary: Data hidden inside JSON columns is invisible to every schema-level question, and is often where the interesting fields live.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Which glossary terms do these columns probably mean?
terms.description: Suggestions rather than assignments, drawn from column names, any matched Data Classes and any matched reference-data sets, and published as Egeria SemanticAnnotations for a steward to accept or reject.
terms.summary: Columns bound to agreed terms are the difference between a catalogued database and an understandable one.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Which low-cardinality columns conform to a known reference-data set, and which should become one?
terms.description: Columns whose n_distinct falls under a threshold have their distinct values compared against every Egeria ValidValueSet. A full match becomes ValidValuesAssignment advice; a partial match raises an RFA listing the unmatched values; no match at all raises an RFA proposing a new ValidValueSet carrying the values.
terms.summary: Uncontrolled code columns are where data quality quietly fails, and they are cheap to find.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Which resources cover similar subjects, grain and period or places — could one stand in for this one, or this one for them?
terms.description: Scope similarity is lens fit (design §16.5): derive a lens from this resource's declared or measured DataScope, DataGrain and subject terms and run the fit against every other resource's stored scope — no new survey, a query over stored measurements. Runs both ways, so a resource that fails one investigation's lens can still match another (§16.5 point 5). Also the mechanism behind 'is something like this already productised' (§16.7 5′). The answer is a relation per scope axis — subject, population (which customers: pre-sales vs post-sales), space, time, grain, structure — each same / contains / contained_by / overlaps / disjoint / not_established, with 'can one stand in for the other' and 'is one a subset of the other' derived from them (design §16.8). Two 'customer' databases are never called similar on subject alone: an undeclared population axis renders not_established.
terms.summary: Whether a resource can substitute for another is a question of scope — subject, grain, coverage in time and space — not of content; this is what a consumer choosing between two datasets actually asks.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Which resources have similar content — code, documentation or data values — and how does this one differ?
terms.description: Content similarity over embeddings of code, documents and sampled data (pgvector). Complements scope similarity (which needs declared or measured scope) and structural similarity (which needs a schema). Design §16.7 5′ and the coverage audit's similarity item: content finds candidates; scope fit ranks them.
terms.summary: Finds candidates by what they contain, including resources whose scope and purpose were never declared — the only similarity that works before any curation.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Which schemas carry the data, and which are system, empty or staging?
terms.description: Derived from the same catalog read as the size question — object counts and sizes per schema, plus name conventions. Cheap, whole-database, no row data.
terms.summary: Knowing which schemas matter stops every later analysis from paying to profile scratch and system objects.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.

terms.display_name: Which tables have no primary key, no foreign key, no comment, unused indexes, or names that break the convention?
terms.description: Check-granular in the same shape as the repository conventions analysis: each defect is its own named check so an assessment can cite it and a subscription can watch it. All of it reads the catalog, including pg_stat_user_indexes for indexes nothing uses.
terms.summary: These are the specific, fixable defects behind a vague sense that a database is badly kept.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Which tables would a consumer start with?
terms.description: A ranking rather than a measure: foreign-key in-degree, row counts, presence of comments and read activity from the scan counters, combined into a short starting list. Zero new fetch.
terms.summary: A hundred-table database with no entry point is functionally undiscoverable, however well it is catalogued.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Discovery.

terms.display_name: Who can read and write what — roles, grants, superusers, PUBLIC grants, and are sensitive columns readable broadly?
terms.description: pg_roles, role_table_grants and pg_default_acl give the access half and already have an analysis. The sensitivity half needs column-level Data Class matching, and the question is the cross of the two — which is why a broad PUBLIC grant on an unremarkable table and the same grant on a table of personal data read identically today.
terms.summary: Access is only half an answer; access crossed with sensitivity is the half anyone acts on.
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

terms.display_name: Who owns this resource (accountable owner), and who administers it?
terms.description: repository_health alone answers 'is it maintained', not 'by whom' — the two questions returned the same text until chaoss_metrics, built on project_commits, gave this one its own source.
terms.summary: Are they reputable?
terms.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Scouting.
